item.title: 19 mil reproducciones · 61 reacciones | Itchy skin? Burning eyes? Sleepless nights? Awkward spots? Not all side effects are obvious. They can range from a skin rash, headache or upset stomach to changes in sleep, mood or other unexpected symptoms. Some side effects appear soon after starting a medicine; others may develop after prolonged use, a change in dose, taking several medicines together or even after treatment has stopped. If your medicine is making you feel worse, tell your doctor! Help make medicines safer for everyone! | World Health Organization (WHO)

item.description: More than half of working carers in Hong Kong have never used the family-friendly measures offered by their companies, a study has found, sparking calls from experts to change workplace cultures to prevent carers being stigmatised. item.title: Star mathematician Ma Xiao leaves the US for China – and a career pivot to AI
item.description: Two years ago, Chinese mathematician Ma Xiao helped crack a century-old puzzle known as Hilbert’s sixth problem. The problem – which has baffled generations of mathematical physicists – centres on an elusive bridge connecting the chaotic frenzy of microscopic atoms with the predictable laws of fluid motion. The breakthrough, published in the Annals of Mathematics, helped propel Ma’s collaborator Deng Yu to the 2026 Fields Medal – the discipline’s highest honour – and secured Ma a coveted faculty... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: El papa "regresa a casa": así será la gira de Leon XIV por Uruguay, Argentina y Perú
item.description: León XIV tiene previsto iniciar este viernes 6 de noviembre uno de los viajes al extranjero más ambiciosos de un pontífice en décadas: visitar Uruguay, Argentina y su país de adopción, Perú, a pesar de haber sido operado recientemente de cáncer de pulmón. El papa llevará en su primera gira latinoamericana un mensaje centrado en la defensa de la vida, el apoyo a los más vulnerables y la reducción de las desigualdades. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Pennsylvania woman treated for breast cancer had rare lymphoma; court allows family's lawsuit

item.title: France's dermatology crisis: Patients desperate for appointments
item.description: Around 200,000 cases of skin cancer are diagnosed in France every year. Yet as more and more patients seek medical advice, getting an appointment with a dermatologist is becoming increasingly difficult. Half the country's dermatologists are nearing retirement, and only around 100 new specialists are trained up each year. Faced with this growing shortage, some are coming up with innovative solutions. FRANCE 24's Aurore Dupuis and Sonia Baritello report. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: Sonia BARITELLO
